questions.question: Explain the difference between latitude and longitude and describe South Africa's position.
questions.expected_answer: Lines of latitude run across the globe parallel to the equator and measure how far north or south a place is, from zero to ninety degrees. Lines of longitude run from pole to pole and measure how far east or west of the Greenwich Meridian a place is, from zero to one hundred and eighty degrees. South Africa is south of the equator and east of Greenwich, so it is in the Southern and Eastern Hemispheres, roughly between twenty-two and thirty-five degrees south and sixteen and thirty-three degrees east.

questions.question: Explain why a line scale is more useful than a word scale on a photocopied map, and describe one method of measuring distance.
questions.expected_answer: A line scale is drawn on the map and changes size with it, so it stays correct when the map is enlarged or reduced, while a word scale becomes wrong. With the paper strip method, you mark both places on the edge of a strip, put the first mark on the zero of the line scale and read the distance at the second mark.

questions.question: Describe Mapungubwe as the first state in southern Africa, referring to its king, its classes and its trade.
questions.expected_answer: From about 1220 to 1300 AD, Mapungubwe was ruled by a sacred king who lived apart on the hilltop and was believed to be close to the ancestors and the rain. Society had distinct classes: royals on the hill, important people near it and ordinary people in the valley. Gold objects symbolised royal power. The king controlled trade, sending gold and ivory on foot to the coast in exchange for glass beads and cloth from across the Indian Ocean.
